still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it. That is now true even of Novo's own authorised generic, which sells for a small fraction of it.

The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there. Zepbound and Wegovy injectable maintenance on TrumpRx stays in the $279–349 band set in May 2029.
The FDA has approved no generic tirzepatide, and no generic oral semaglutide. The semaglutide generics that exist are all weekly injectables.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels. MariTide is still the only monthly incretin, and no implant is on the US market.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: 31.5% ever-used − 22.8% current = 8.7% of adults who used and are off now. 44% of 31.5 = 13.9 points have cycled. ~11.5 are current users on at least a second course (~50% of current users, slightly lower than 2030 because the 2032 generic and Medicare/Medicaid cohort is new). ~2.4 cycled and are off again. ~6.3 stopped once and never restarted. Cheap generics raised restart rates (now ~45–50% within a year) but did not change one-year persistence (~one-third). Age check: 0.20×12 + 0.33×22.5 + 0.24×32 + 0.23×23 = 2.4 + 7.43 + 7.68 + 5.29 = 22.8. Income check: (26 + 23 + 19.4)/3 ≈ 22.8. About 22.8% of ~270M adults is ~61.6M users. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare ~26% (~16.0M: ~13.6M aged 65+ and ~2.4M disabled or ESRD under 65), Medicaid ~12% (~7.4M, up from 3.3M after the generic-incretin coverage mandate took effect in Jan 2032), commercial ~21% (~12.9M), legitimate cash ~29% (~17.9M: ~10M generic semaglutide at $39–69, ~5M TrumpRx orals, ~3M direct tirzepatide or MariTide), gray market ~12% (~7.4M). Public payers together (~23.4M, 38%) are now the largest payer category. The top–bottom gap narrowed from 11 points to 6.6 because Medicaid and $49 generics reached the bottom third, but bottom-third users are disproportionately on generic semaglutide and gray product, not tirzepatide or retatrutide. Off-drug populations: ~23.5M adults used and are off now (8.7%), and adult obesity is ~32.6%. ~19% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug. Many are now people who could afford it and decline it, a group the 'Unassisted' movement claims to speak for. Pediatric: ~1.5% of under-18s, ~3.2% of 12–17s and ~0.35% of 6–11s. Children's use grew mainly through Medicaid EPSDT and generic liraglutide or semaglutide. Growth stalled in the 11 states with 2032 restriction laws.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The March 2031 appropriations package lifted the Part D and Medicaid weight-loss exclusion for 'lowest-cost' incretins, meaning generic injectable semaglutide and generic liraglutide, effective Jan 2032. The criteria are BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity. Brands remain available only through the diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, behind prior authorisation. Medicare spend arithmetic: ~7.0M on generic semaglutide (≈5.1M new obesity-benefit users plus ≈1.9M switched from brand) × ~$55 net × 12 ≈ $4.6B. ~9.0M on brands (tirzepatide incl. ~1.9M dementia-route, orals, retatrutide, MariTide) × ~$230 net × 12 ≈ $24.8B. Total ≈ $29.4B a year, roughly flat against 2030's $29.7B with ~6M more users. Medicaid arithmetic: ~5.6M generic × ~$40 net × 12 ≈ $2.7B plus ~1.8M brand × ~$245 × 12 ≈ $5.3B, total ≈ $8.0B federal and state combined. CBO scored the change at ~$26B over 2032–41: ≈5.5M added Medicare users at maturity × ~$55 × 12 ≈ $3.6B a year gross, less modest medical offsets, ramping in.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide is $4–30 a month, and Chinese tirzepatide analogues sell widely in markets without patents. Canadian generics run CAD 40–80. India and China still supply most global volume, including most of the API in US generic semaglutide.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Generic injectable semaglutide (six ANDA holders sharing first-filer exclusivity, plus Novo's authorised generic) launched in Jan 2032 at ~$149. It was $39–69 cash at warehouse clubs, Cost Plus-style pharmacies and chains by Q3 2032. Employer coverage rose from 36% to 39%, almost entirely as generic-only tiers. Tirzepatide and retatrutide are excluded or step-edited behind generic semaglutide at most employers. Metabolic tracks shrank from ~4.5M to ~3.6M enrollees, all inside the ~12.9M commercial users. ~2.1M of them are on clinic-administered MariTide. MariTide totals ~3.2M users across payers. Access is now an income-floor question: $49 a month is trivial in Charlotte and a utility bill in Dayton, which is why Medicaid matters. The efficacy gap is now the price gap. Generic semaglutide (~15%) is cheap. Tirzepatide (~21%) and retatrutide (~24%) are not, and that gap drives the gray market. Indian-vial and counterfeit semaglutide volume fell by about half after generics launched. The resurgence is compounded tirzepatide and retatrutide ('personalised' with B12 or glycine) from 503A pharmacies and offshore fillers, and fake 'monthly semaglutide depot', all sold through telehealth 'metabolic wellness' platforms at $89–179. That is ~4.6M of the ~7.4M gray users.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic; generic semaglutide injectable since Jan 2032)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular agonist, weekly injectable (amycretin, approved Feb 2031)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; the extension to adults 60+ without CVD received a complete response letter in Jul 2031)
smoking and vaping cessation in adults, as adjunct to counselling (oral semaglutide, Nov 2031)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction (oral semaglutide AUD sNDA filed Jan 2032 after a modestly positive phase 3; decision expected 2033)
nicotine cessation using cheap generic injectable semaglutide instead of the approved oral
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, cash-paid
microdosing and 'dose-down' maintenance for steadiness or, increasingly, to reduce flatness
semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity (off-label; restricted by law in 11 states)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Amycretin (filed Oct 2029) was approved Feb 2031 as a weekly injectable at ~22% weight loss. Uptake is mostly commercial with prior authorisation. Tirzepatide's dementia sNDA for adults 60+ without CVD received a complete response in Jul 2031. The FDA wants the confirmatory trial, which reads out 2033, so Medicare's dementia route stays limited to the CVD population (~1.9M). The nicotine driver is an existing product in a new indication: Novo filed oral semaglutide for smoking and vaping cessation in Jan 2031 on two phase 3 trials (about 8–10 points higher continuous abstinence at 24 weeks vs placebo), and it was approved Nov 2031. The monthly driver is realised by MariTide's spread to ~3.2M users, including Part D under CV codes from 2032. No implant has reached phase 3, and no other monthly product is approved. Generic semaglutide is injectable only. Oral formulation patents run later, and tirzepatide's patents run to the mid-2030s. Bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts filed in mid-2032, so there is no decision before 2033. The global incretin market is ~$150B (2031): volume is up sharply, and US semaglutide revenue is down ~60% after generic entry.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. New generic-semaglutide starters on Medicaid and Medicare show the familiar early-titration peak. MariTide's early vomiting remains higher than the weekly drugs'.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
No causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Litigation now centres on exocrine insufficiency, and generic makers have joined as defendants.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years, and ~1.45 in people who have cycled three or more times. The Medicare obesity benefit added ~5M mostly older, mostly untrained starters, so absolute fracture counts are expected to rise even with stable relative risk.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained. The DXA code is covered once at Part D initiation under the 2031 law, and generic labels carry the same warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal, including in the smoking-cessation trials, which monitored for it specifically.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: An FDA postmarketing interim analysis (2032) is consistent with ~7% clinically meaningful anhedonia vs ~3% in controls, dose-related, ~10% on retatrutide. Mild 'evenness' is reported by a large minority. Self-directed dose reduction and drug holidays are now common responses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling. FDA patient-information language on 'mood and enjoyment changes' is under review.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Cheap generics shortened gaps between courses, which moved regain toward a 'sawtooth' pattern.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins chronic-therapy framing and the 2031 coverage law's 'continuous therapy' language.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users; fat-soluble vitamins linked to EPI in long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel recommended in professional guidance. A 2031 label update added monitoring language.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Further Danish and US follow-up holds ~4 per 1,000 person-years vs ~2 in matched controls after year 5 on semaglutide. Partial reversibility was seen in a small cohort that stopped. Tirzepatide data are still too thin to rule in or out. No new signal emerged.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC concluded Mar 2031 with an EU semaglutide label update. The FDA added EPI to semaglutide (and generic) Warnings in Aug 2031. Class labelling for other agents is still undecided.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About ten years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. The first pediatric bone-density interim (liraglutide 6–11) reported in 2032 with no clear deficit at 2 years, too early to conclude.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric postmarketing requirements continue. Eleven states' 2032 laws add specialist-only prescribing below 12.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Counterfeit semaglutide pens fell as generics undercut them. Harms shifted to compounded retatrutide and tirzepatide: dosing errors from unit-of-measure confusion, and endotoxin contamination in two 2032 offshore lots. Poison-centre calls are ~3.5× 2025 levels, down slightly from 2030.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters to ~40 telehealth platforms and 503A pharmacies (Apr 2032). State-board telehealth in-person rules in 11 states. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

food_and_beverage.state: About 40% of US households now have a user, up from 33%. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~10–12% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~9%. The 2032 Medicaid and Medicare wave hit exactly the value-pack zip codes that had held up, so private-label snack volume finally turned down in lower-income markets. Premium protein lines are crowding out value lines on discount shelves, and whey prices remain elevated. In a small counter-trend, 'Unassisted'-branded heritage bakeries and full-fat dairy are growing in Nashville, Brooklyn and Asheville.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~13% from 2025 and beer ~8%. The incremental 2032 loss is concentrated in older, lower-income drinkers newly on Medicare and Medicaid generic semaglutide. Bar closures continue across the Midwest. Non-alcoholic lines are growing. Tobacco is the new adjacent casualty: after the Nov 2031 cessation approval and cheap off-label generic use, cigarette volumes fell ~6% in 2032 against a ~4% trend, and Altria's guidance cites incretins for the first time.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to down slightly. Value menus at QSRs in lower-income markets lost the volume they had gained since 2027. Casual-dining check sizes are still shrinking. Small-plate and protein menus are universal. A niche of 'long table' restaurants marketed to the unmedicated is growing in a handful of cities.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists are still contracting, and the 2032 public-coverage wave removed part of their remaining core customer. Resale and stretch serve cyclers. 'Soft-strong' cuts marketed to the Unassisted aesthetic appear at a few premium brands.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Medicare Advantage plans now bundle resistance-training benefits against the fracture warning. Budget gyms run 'GLP-1 strength' classes for older members. Premium DXA-and-coaching clubs plateaued as the lifted body became more common.

insurance.state: Commercial pharmacy trend fell to ~+3% in 2032 as generic semaglutide replaced brand spend. Employers re-added generic-only weight coverage (39%). Adherence differentials persist under the 2027 guidance but are used less after the EEOC finding. Part D premiums rose again for 2032, and Medicare incretin spend held near ~$29B because volume growth roughly offset generic substitution.

pharma.state: Novo's US semaglutide revenue is down ~60% after generic entry. It leans on its authorised generic, the oral, the nicotine indication and amycretin. Lilly still grows on tirzepatide and retatrutide, though the dementia CRL dented expectations. Amgen's MariTide reached ~3.2M users. US generic makers (Teva, Viatris, Sandoz, Dr. Reddy's, others) earn thin margins on volume. Compounding and telehealth platforms are a ~$7B shadow market.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Thinness no longer signals income, because $49 and Medicaid put it within reach of almost everyone. The signals now are which drug you take and whether you chose to take any. A lean, muscled body still reads as covered and coached. A thinning body over 55 in Dayton or Tulsa reads as 'on the Medicare shot'. A deliberately soft, strong, unmedicated body in its twenties reads, increasingly, as a choice and as a kind of money.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The 2030 regainers, bottom-third women aged 50–64, are the largest group of new Medicaid starters in 2032, and the 'second thinning' is visible in church halls and on home-health rosters across Ohio and Kentucky. In the top tier, the efficacy ladder (generic semaglutide → tirzepatide → retatrutide) has replaced the drug/no-drug line as the status marker. In Nashville, East Austin and Brooklyn, among affluent 18–29s, 'Unassisted' has become an identity: never-medicated or proudly quit, with its own aesthetic of full plates, sourdough, soft-strong bodies and 'born hungry' merch.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals remain shorter in medicated households. The Unassisted movement stages 'long tables', multi-hour dinners where phones and pens are checked at the door, as a ritual of visible appetite. The Bread Alone fasting network persists in Oklahoma and Arkansas and allied with Unassisted on the 2032 state laws, despite opposite views of eating. School lunch fights now include whether children on drugs should be served smaller portions.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added an 'Unassisted' badge alongside 'lean-mass verified', and the two audiences barely overlap. Couples on weekly generic schedule shared 'off weeks' around trips and anniversaries. Couples where one partner is on clinic-administered MariTide cannot do that, and some switch back to weekly generic to regain control over timing.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has become a stance as well as a symptom. For the medicated majority of older adults, it is managed noise. For Unassisted, it is authenticity and pleasure, and its critics call that a luxury of the young and genetically lucky. For the newly covered poor, the return of not being hungry is mostly described as relief.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7% of users vs ~3% of controls (FDA interim), ~10% on retatrutide. With ~61.6M users, that implies roughly 2.5M excess cases nationally. A much larger share report mild 'flatness', and self-directed dose reduction or periodic drug holidays are now common practice, reported by roughly a third of long-term users in survey data.
interior_life.framing: Flatness is now a common complaint: talked about on late-night TV, managed with 'dose-down' maintenance and 'off weeks', and treated by clinicians as a dose-related side effect to titrate around. HR quietly removed 'steadiness' from competency language after the 2031 EEOC finding. Unassisted frames it as the reason to refuse the drug entirely.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Metabolic tracks shrank to ~3.6M enrollees, and adherence metrics have mostly disappeared from promotion files at the Columbus-corridor logistics firms and call-centre operators named in the EEOC charges. Clinic-administered MariTide persists because it is convenient and covered, but enrollees now ask for dose reductions before review periods. Some bring 'off-week' requests to managers the way they once requested PTO. The Texas and Indiana state plans still report adherence.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Flat' fiction has gone mainstream, and a network sitcom about a couple on alternating drug holidays is in its second season. Unmuted's off nights folded partly into Unassisted's long tables and live shows, which skew younger and richer than Unmuted's Detroit and Baltimore crowds. Sportsbook handle per account keeps falling. Spicy, loud, sour food remains a genre.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Drug holidays are now routine couples' negotiation. Therapists report the 'parallel lives' pattern easing among couples who moved from monthly back to weekly dosing, and persisting where an employer clinic administers the dose.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The coverage law passed on a cost argument (generics) with bipartisan votes. The restriction wave passed on a child-protection argument pushed by MAHA legislators, Unassisted organisers and the Bread Alone churches. Tobacco-state delegations (Kentucky, North Carolina) quietly opposed Part D coverage of the cessation indication. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence. The visible split is now between older medicated voters, for whom the drug is a Medicare benefit to defend, and the young unmedicated, for whom it is pharma.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal posture is mixed: pro-access on generics and coverage, pro-speed on routine approvals (amycretin, the nicotine indication), cautious on dementia (CRL), and newly aggressive on advertising. In Jun 2032 an FDA final rule ended the 'adequate provision' shortcut for broadcast ads, which in practice took incretin TV ads off the air. PhRMA's First Amendment challenge is pending. Eleven states passed restrictions in 2032.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The March 2031 law makes generic incretins a Part D and mandatory Medicaid covered drug for obesity from Jan 2032. It is the first statutory obesity-drug coverage since the 2003 exclusion. TrumpRx continues. There are no mandates to take the drug. The 2027 30% wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged in law. Employer use of adherence data declined after the EEOC finding, but PBM, app and clinic records still flow to wellness vendors under consent. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition brand coverage on adherence and BMI progress; generic coverage carries no such condition under federal law.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE rules are unchanged, as is the Army oral pilot. DOT still has not ruled on drivers. The EEOC's Sep 2031 reasonable-cause finding against two logistics employers (ADA disability-related inquiry) went to conciliation, with no litigation yet.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Most API for US generic semaglutide comes from India and China, so US price collapse now depends on the supply chain Washington spent years trying to police. US–India talks folded generic API security into the same agenda as mail enforcement. The Danish price-gap row faded once US generic prices came within ~2–5× of India's.

events.event: Novo Nordisk settles the last Paragraph IV suits over injectable semaglutide, licensing six generic makers to launch in January 2032 and announcing its own authorised generic

Congress's March appropriations package lifts the Part D and Medicaid exclusion for 'lowest-cost' obesity drugs from January 2032; CBO scores it at about $26B over ten years, citing generic semaglutide pricing

EEOC finds reasonable cause in ADA charges against two Columbus-area logistics firms over adherence-linked promotion; within months large employers drop 'steadiness' from competency language as 'off weeks' go mainstream
FDA approves oral semaglutide as an adjunct for smoking and vaping cessation; Altria later cites incretins in guidance as cigarette volumes fall faster than trend

With generic semaglutide at $39–69 at warehouse clubs, FDA sends warning letters to some 40 telehealth platforms and compounders selling 'personalised' retatrutide, tirzepatide and fake 'monthly depot' semaglutide to an estimated 4–5 million customers; Amgen reports 3.2M on its genuine monthly MariTide

Eleven states led by Tennessee, Oklahoma and Utah pass laws limiting under-12 prescribing to pediatric endocrinologists and requiring in-person visits before telehealth starts; the same month an FDA rule effectively ends incretin TV ads, after lobbying by the 'Unassisted' movement and MAHA legislators

open_tensions: The public payer now funds tens of millions of continuous-therapy users, many of them old, untrained and newly on drug. The fracture warning and the 5-year EPI signal apply to exactly the exposure the coverage law treats as permanent.

Generic semaglutide made thinness cheap, but the efficacy ladder did not get cheaper. Tirzepatide and retatrutide sit at $279+ or behind prior authorisation, and ~4.6M people fill the gap with compounded next-gen peptides that the FDA warns about and states cannot police across borders.

The restriction wave and the Unassisted movement frame children and young adults as people to protect from the drug, while Medicaid EPSDT pulls more low-income children onto it. Pediatric use is diverging by state and by class, and the bone data are still years away.

Tirzepatide's dementia claim for people without heart disease is waiting on a 2033 readout. If it is approved, Medicare's flat ~$29B incretin spend will turn sharply upward on brand prices just as Part D premiums are already rising.

prose.headline: The $49 Shot: Medicare Pays, Teenagers Refuse, and the Thin Body Stops Meaning Money
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2032 almost one American adult in four takes an incretin drug, and nearly a third have tried one. The rise of the past two years did not come from a better molecule. It came from an older one getting cheap. In January, six generic makers and Novo Nordisk's own authorised-generic arm began selling injectable semaglutide under a settlement signed two years earlier. By late summer a month's supply cost $49 at a warehouse club. The box of branded Wegovy still says $1,349, and the TrumpRx pill still starts at $149. Neither number matters much any more.

Congress moved first. In March 2031, counting on the generic price, a spending package lifted the exclusion that had kept weight-loss drugs out of Medicare and Medicaid since 2003, but only for the cheapest drugs. The change took effect in January. Within a year about sixteen million Medicare beneficiaries and seven million Medicaid enrollees were on a drug. Public programmes are now the largest payer. Because cheap generics replaced expensive brands for the patients Medicare already covered, its incretin bill barely moved, at about $29 billion. The brands remain behind prior authorisation on the old codes. In July 2031 the FDA declined, for now, to extend tirzepatide's dementia claim to people without heart disease, which kept that bill from climbing.

The effect on bodies is easiest to see in the places the previous decade skipped. In Dayton, Louisville and Tulsa, women in their fifties who regained after losing coverage in 2028 are thinning again on Medicaid. Thin no longer signals money. What still signals money is the rung on the ladder: generic semaglutide takes off about fifteen per cent, tirzepatide over twenty, Lilly's retatrutide nearly a quarter, and the two newer drugs cost five or six times as much. That gap supports a gray market that has grown back in a different form. Counterfeit Ozempic is mostly gone, undercut by the real thing. In its place, about four and a half million people buy 'personalised' compounded retatrutide or fake monthly depots through telehealth wellness sites for around $129. In April the FDA sent forty warning letters. The sites changed their names.

A monthly shot does exist. Amgen's MariTide reaches about three million people, many of them through employer clinics. Monthly dosing has made the old weekly decision automatic, and that is now something patients complain about. The flatness some users feel has become an ordinary complaint, the stuff of sitcoms and call-ins. After the EEOC found in 2031 that two Columbus logistics firms had tied promotions to adherence, 'steadiness' quietly disappeared from HR competency documents. People now talk about off weeks and dose-downs the way they talk about sleep. Some MariTide patients ask to switch back to the weekly generic just to get the calendar back.

In November 2031 the FDA approved oral semaglutide for quitting cigarettes and vapes. Many smokers skipped the branded pill and used the $49 injection off-label. Altria now names the drugs in its guidance, and the bars of the Midwest keep closing.

In Nashville, East Austin and Brooklyn, the reaction has an aesthetic. Young people who could easily afford the drug call themselves Unassisted. They host long-table dinners, eat sourdough, sell 'born hungry' shirts, and favour a body that is soft and strong. Their critics call this the newest luxury good. Their politics joined those of MAHA legislators and Oklahoma's fasting churches, and in June eleven states limited prescriptions for children under twelve to specialists and required an in-person visit before any telehealth start. The FDA, separately, ended incretin TV advertising. Meanwhile Medicaid's pediatric rules keep pulling poorer children onto the drug in the other thirty-nine states.

The exocrine warning is on the semaglutide label now, and nothing new has been found. From a distance the country looks thinner and calmer than it was, and it is now publicly funded to stay on these drugs for good.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Harper, fifty-seven, keeps the pen in the butter compartment because her granddaughter can't reach it there. Sunday is shot day. The box says Ohio Medicaid, generic, $3.40 copay, and on the side, in small type, the name of a company in Hyderabad.

She does it standing at the counter before church, in the soft part below the navel. She lost thirty-one pounds on the Bridge in 2027, gained back thirty-eight after the agency dropped her hours, and since March has lost twenty-two again. Her scrubs from 2027 fit, in the wrong order.

At Greater Love the coffee hour is quieter than it used to be. Half the women her age hold their plates the same way, with one cookie on a napkin, mostly for the look of it. Pastor's wife asks if she's still on the menthols. Denise says four a day, down from a pack, and she didn't even ask it to do that.

In the afternoon she sees her client Mr. Okafor, eighty-one, also on the Medicare shot, and drives him to the strength class at the Y, because his plan pays for it now and the fracture sheet on his fridge says to go.

Her daughter Kayla calls from Nashville at dinner. Kayla works at a bakery whose window says UNASSISTED, and she sends pictures of bread like other people send pictures of babies.

"You don't have to be on it forever, Mama."

"I know it."

Denise eats half a pork chop and wraps the rest. She isn't hungry, she isn't sad, and she isn't anything in particular. She sets an alarm for next Sunday.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Cheap generics raised restart rates (now ~45–50% within a year) but did not change one-year persistence (~one-third).
least_plausible_claims.why: Higher restart rates should raise the cycled share and the share of current users on a second course. The world instead holds `cycled_off_and_on_pct` at exactly 44 and says the second-course share fell from ~53% to ~50%, so the stated mechanism contradicts the reconciled figures (magnitude and mechanism).

least_plausible_claims.quote: Novo filed oral semaglutide for smoking and vaping cessation in Jan 2031 on two phase 3 trials (about 8–10 points higher continuous abstinence at 24 weeks vs placebo), and it was approved Nov 2031.
least_plausible_claims.why: The parent lists no nicotine filing and no nicotine phase 3. Under the envelope's approval rule, a phase 3 product that files in this window cannot be approved earlier than 12 months after the filing, and Jan to Nov 2031 is 10 months (magnitude).

least_plausible_claims.quote: CBO scored the change at ~$26B over 2032–41: ≈5.5M added Medicare users at maturity × ~$55 × 12 ≈ $3.6B a year gross, less modest medical offsets, ramping in.
least_plausible_claims.why: The arithmetic does not reach the score. $3.6B a year gross over ten years is about $36B, and 'modest' offsets cannot remove ~28% of it. The score also omits the mandatory Medicaid expansion (~$2.7B a year generic spend on 5.6M users), so the budget figure is under-reconciled (magnitude).

rationale.badness: This is a mixed world, with access widened but new costs. Cheap generics and Medicaid/Medicare coverage narrow the income gap (top 26 vs bottom 19.4). Anhedonia (~2.5M excess cases), a rising absolute fracture burden among ~5M untrained older starters, a ~$7B compounded gray market with contamination harms, and divergent pediatric use by state and class keep it from being benign.
